author: bd-spin/bd-spin-20260512T000441Z-1660907
text:
/do-beads run 2026-05-12 hit an unexpected design gap.

The bead description says "spin up jmap_mail_server::memory::MemoryBackend behind an in-process axum/hyper test server". Two missing pieces block that plan:

1. `crate-jmap-mail-server/Cargo.toml` has NO axum or hyper dep. The crate is the dispatcher-handlers library (RFC 8621 method handlers + MailBackend trait + reference MemoryBackend); it has no HTTP transport surface. There is no `jmap-mail-server::serve_axum()` style entry point to wire into the example.

2. `crate-jmap-mail-client/Cargo.toml` has NO `jmap-mail-server` dev-dep, only `wiremock = "0.6"` and tokio.

Three options:

(A) Use wiremock with a hand-written Mailbox/get JSON fixture, like the landed `crate-jmap-base-client/examples/session_fetch.rs` from .17.2. ~80 LOC, single-session, meets all four acceptance criteria. Trade-off: contradicts the parent .17's stated design intent ("wrap the public reference impls with thin example narratives"). The example demonstrates JmapClient -> wire JSON -> response parsing, but not the live reference backend.

(B) Build an axum bridge inline in the example: pull in axum/tower/hyper as dev-deps of jmap-mail-client, mount POST /api -> JmapMailDispatcher::dispatch and GET /.well-known/jmap -> static session JSON, bind to a localhost ephemeral port, point JmapClient at it. ~150-200 LOC. Closer to the "real backend" narrative but the axum-wiring overhead dominates the per-method demo.

(C) File a new bead for "add `jmap_mail_server::server::serve_axum(...)` or similar HTTP-bridge helper to jmap-mail-server", make .17.4 depend on it. The bridge would also be useful for integration tests. Bigger scope — a full feature, not a 50-80 LOC example.

Recommendation: (A). Matches the workspace's already-landed example template (.17.2 + .17.3), single-session, meets acceptance verbatim. The "live MemoryBackend" framing in the parent .17 bead body looks aspirational — it pre-dated noticing that the server crates have no HTTP surface yet. A future bd:JMAP-* could revisit once an HTTP-bridge helper lands (option C as a sequel).

Mark: pick A/B/C and drop the human label. /do-beads will pick it up the next run.

Note: JMAP-sc1b.17.5 (chat-client sse_listen/ws_loop) has the same gap on jmap-chat-server. Resolution decision should apply to both.
